name: Unrest
label: Simple Machines
lede: Mark Robinson started a record label in high school, made his band its house act, and by 1993 had a 4AD box set of 7-inches to show for a rule about never playing the same song twice.

eras.title: Never the same song twice
eras.text: Wakefield High School, Arlington, Virginia: Mark Robinson, Tim Moran and Phil Krauth start a band with one rule, no repeats. The records swing between punk, funk and noise, and the label that puts them out is Robinson's own.

years.cap: Tim Moran, Phil Krauth and Mark Robinson
yt: Mark Robinson rates Unrest: the road to Imperial, 1985-1992
years.h: A high-schooler starts a label, and Unrest is its band
years.p: [[Mark Robinson|fc1a1e50-b6f7-431f-834b-d1441e54dcb7]] founds Teenbeat Records while still in school; the self-titled Unrest cassette comes out May 1, 1985.
years.xp:
Teen-Beat dates the band to 1983 and Wakefield High School in Arlington, Virginia, with Robinson on guitar and vocals, Moran on bass and Phil Krauth on drums. Wikipedia describes the early Unrest as an experiment built on never playing the same song twice, with punk, funk and Ennio Morricone in the mix.

A second Teenbeat LP, Lisa Carol Freemont, followed on August 29 of the same year.

years.cap: Mark Robinson and Phil Krauth recording Malcolm X Park at Noise N.Y., 1988
years.h: Malcolm X Park is the first Unrest LP with a distributor
years.p: Named for a D.C. park, it comes out on Teenbeat with Caroline behind it.

eras.title: Bridget Cross plugs in the bass
eras.text: Bridget Cross takes the bass and the songs get lighter and shorter. The white noise, sirens and beeps stay, tucked between the pop.

years.cap: Phil Krauth, Bridget Cross and Mark Robinson, c. 1990
years.h: Bridget Cross takes the bass and Unrest turns toward pop
years.p: By 1990, Wikipedia says, the sound is a "minimalist but lively kind of pop", with [[Bridget Cross|11a8f5ae-5a31-4258-8c4d-87ea4c44c197]] on bass.

years.h: Kustom Karnal Blackxploitation puts pop next to percussion and noise
years.p: Teenbeat and Caroline release it April 6. Avant-garde percussion tracks sit between the pop songs, a mix the band keeps through 1993.

years.h: Unrest and Shudder to Think share a 7-inch
years.p: The split single with fellow D.C. band [[Shudder to Think|5a6e19e0-3ff0-4b3d-869e-3c539d6d8707]] is one of a run of 7-inches Robinson puts out on Teenbeat.

years.cap: Bridget Cross at the Fun City studio, New York
years.h: Thirteen days at Fun City in New York for Imperial f.f.r.r.
years.p: Unrest records July 15 to 27, 1991, with [[Wharton Tiers|de3636ee-5022-462b-b427-34be9674f281]] at the board and Krauth and Robinson sharing production.

years.h: Unrest lands on Simple Machines' Fortune Cookie Prize
years.p: Simple Machines, a label run out of an Arlington house, puts the band on its compilation, the start of Unrest's link to that scene.
years.xp: Simple Machines also put out the Inclined Plane singles series (with [[Tsunami|fea43e99-c4d5-4dac-9c27-868e864c6dc2]], [[Superchunk|61653550-fd9b-4401-8248-44f2d064d384]], [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]] and Unrest) and the Machines 1990–1993 compilation, per the label's discography on Wikipedia.

eras.title: Imperial puts them on the map, 4AD gives them a box set
eras.text: Imperial f.f.r.r. lands on Spin's 1992 list, 4AD starts putting out the EPs, and Perfect Teeth becomes the best seller. The EPs in between hold up next to the albums.

years.cap: Phil Krauth, Bridget Cross and Mark Robinson at the Chaos House, Knoxville, Tennessee, January 1992
yt: Cherry Cherry, live in London, September 2, 1992
years.h: Imperial f.f.r.r. ends up 8th on Spin's list for 1992
years.p: No.6 and Teenbeat release it March 16. Alternative Press later puts it at number 73 on its 90 greatest albums of the 90s.
years.xp: Pitchfork later gave it 8.2 out of 10. The UK edition on Guernica added four bonus tracks, a 2005 remaster added nine more, alternate versions and unreleased material, and a vinyl reissue followed in 2009.

years.h: Isabel Bishop EP is Unrest's first for 4AD
years.p: Teenbeat and 4AD release it July 21, named for the American painter, and Ivo Watts-Russell's label starts its run with the band.

years.src: It's Psychedelic Baby · Wikipedia: Perfect Teeth
years.h: Unrest cuts about 20 songs at Pachyderm in five days
years.p: [[Brian Paulson|65f13d3b-ddd6-4b33-8ab7-366ee7fb63c4]], who had worked on Slint's Spiderland, engineers the March 1993 sessions in Minnesota. Eleven songs make Perfect Teeth.
years.xp:
Pachyderm was a remote compound with residential rooms and a heated indoor pool, and Nirvana had just finished In Utero there. The drums went down in the main room instead of an isolation booth.

Robinson told It's Psychedelic Baby that "the real creation of the album came in song selection and sequencing." A 30-minute track called "Hydro" was judged too long and left off.

years.h: Cath Carroll, the second EP named for a person
years.p: Teenbeat and 4AD release it June 23, about six weeks before the album, with an official video for the title track.

years.cap: Mark Robinson, Bridget Cross and Phil Krauth, c. 1993
yt: Cath Carroll, live at the 9:30 Club, September 1993
years.h: Perfect Teeth arrives as a box of 7-inches
years.p: 4AD's first pressing is the 7-inch box; CD, 12-inch and cassette follow August 24. Billboard put its sales at about 15,000 in 2010, the most of any Unrest album.
years.xp:
Simon Le Bon of Duran Duran got a production credit after the band joked about asking him. The label then called him, and per Wikipedia he spent two days in the studio and produced nothing.

Reviews split. AllMusic's retrospective called it "the high point of the group's career"; Entertainment Weekly called the guitar work "so lethargic it's almost not there."

years.cap: Phil Krauth, Bridget Cross and Mark Robinson in a London hotel lobby, 1993
years.h: Unrest plays Newcastle, and Teenbeat keeps the tape
years.p: The British tour stops in Newcastle on August 2, 1993; Teenbeat releases the recording as a live album in 2009.
years.xp: Unrest also shared a 1993 split 7-inch with [[Stereolab|f1df0431-9250-4ec8-95d8-f19ce7cf7fb6]] and supported them on tour after Perfect Teeth.

eras.title: Done after Perfect Teeth
eras.text: Unrest dissolves in 1994 with a follow-up called Air Jamaica already sketched. Robinson and Cross start Air Miami instead.

years.big: "We didn't know it was going to be the last album."
years.src: It's Psychedelic Baby · Wikipedia: Unrest (American band)
years.h: Unrest ends with a follow-up already sketched
years.p: Mark Robinson, to It's Psychedelic Baby: he had cover designs ready for Air Jamaica, drawn about a month after Perfect Teeth.
years.xp:
Robinson says the band had no idea Perfect Teeth would be its last, and that preliminary plans and artwork for Air Jamaica already existed.

He and Cross went on to form [[Air Miami|fdc1eb7c-3ad2-4c4a-abf7-81b42f56b989]] with Mike Fellows and Lauren Feldsher.

years.h: Robinson and Cross start Air Miami
years.p: [[Air Miami|fdc1eb7c-3ad2-4c4a-abf7-81b42f56b989]] puts out the Airplane Rider single in 1994 and the LP Me. Me. Me. on 4AD and Teenbeat in 1995, then ends in 1996.

eras.title: Back for a night, a tour, and a few box sets
eras.text: A one-off reunion in 2005, an East Coast run in 2010, and a catalog that keeps getting remastered. Teenbeat, still Robinson's label, keeps the archive open.

years.h: Unrest reunites for one night at the Black Cat
years.p: Teenbeat's 20th-anniversary party, February 24, 2005, in Washington, with Eggs, +/-, True Love Always and others on the bill.
years.xp: Teenbeat later issued the show as a live album in 2009.

years.h: Imperial f.f.r.r. comes back with nine extra tracks
years.p: The 2005 remaster adds alternate versions and unreleased material.

years.h: Bridget Cross records as Maybe It's Reno
years.p: Her self-titled Teenbeat album, out April 22, has Mark Robinson and Phil Krauth on its first seven tracks.

yt: Live at the Bell House, Brooklyn, July 9, 2010
years.h: Unrest tours the East Coast again
years.p: A small run of dates in July, including the Teen-Beat 26th-anniversary show at the Bell House in Brooklyn on July 9.

years.h: Perfect Teeth returns as a colored-vinyl 7-inch box
years.p: Teenbeat's reissue adds bonus tracks and a 24-page booklet of Robinson's studio photographs.

years.h: Perfect Teeth gets an expanded edition and Extra Teeth
years.p: Remastered, with new Chris Bigg art and a 16-page zine of notes from the band and 4AD founder Ivo Watts-Russell. Extra Teeth collects B-sides and rarities.

sources.title: It's Psychedelic Baby: Perfect Teeth Turns 30
